text:
New Jersey put 80 shot attempts on the net to Ottawa's 41, won the even-strength expected goals 2.18 to 1.54, and still lost 4-1. By the share of simulated replays of every shot they win, the Devils deserved the game 66 percent of the time. Linus Ullmark is why they didn't get it. He faced 2.89 expected goals and allowed one, stopping 1.89 more than an average goalie would have, and he took first star.

The game turned in the second period. Ottawa had been outplayed in the first, 0.65 expected goals to 0.46, but Shane Pinto scored nine seconds into the second on a wrist shot the model gave a 12 percent chance. Stephen Halliday made it 2-0 on the power play at 8:40, and Ottawa's chances jumped to 1.34 expected goals against 0.78 for New Jersey. Tim Stützle tipped in a third at 11:10 of the third on a 9 percent chance. Nico Daws gave up three goals on 2.01 expected, a cost of about one goal.

Arseny Gritsyuk finally beat Ullmark at 14:59, set up by Jack Hughes, but Tyler Kleven restored the three-goal margin at 17:53 with a wrist shot the model rated at 44 percent. The Devils also spent 13 minutes in the box to Ottawa's four, and the Senators blocked 30 shots to New Jersey's 10. That is how a team with half the attempts walked out of Prudential Center with the win.
